mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeding 0.0% is a constant condition in the current economic environment, and this accommodative monetary policy level is associated with positive 20-day S&P 500 returns due to low interest rates supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 0.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% signals monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 0.5% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS increase > 0.1% in 3 months) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL change > 3.0% in 12 months) triggers negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to combined monetary tightening and inflationary pressure reducing risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increase > 0.1% in 3 months and CPIAUCSL change > 3.0% in 12 months
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or negative returns occur in < 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.0%), the Federal Reserve implements stimulus measures, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as monetary policy support boosts equity markets.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1000 units is a constant condition in the current environment, and this level of residential construction activity is associated with positive 5-day S&P 500 returns due to strong consumer demand supporting corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST > 1000 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE increase > 0.3pp in 3 months) triggers negative 60-day S&P 500 returns as economic weakness reduces corporate profitability and investor risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.3pp in 3 months over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) and falling housing starts (HOUST < 1200) signals economic contraction, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or negative returns occur in < 40% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns due to reduced manufacturing output and lower corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100 over a 3-year rolling window.
